categories.name: Agent Security, Monitoring, and Safety Evaluation
categories.description: Empirical work on evaluating and safeguarding frontier LLMs and agents: benchmarks for monitors, reward hacking, jailbreaks, misuse classifiers, dangerous-capability and pre-release safety evaluations, and AI control settings against untrusted or sabotaging agents.

categories.name: Agent Monitors, Reward Hacking Benchmarks
categories.description: Benchmarks and tools for overseeing coding/ML agents: monitor and classifier robustness (evasion, long-context degradation, probes, blocking classifiers), auditing agent traces, benchmark hackability and reward hacking, plus agent-automated AI research and red-teaming (autoresearch, post-training, research taste).

categories.name: Jailbreaks, Safeguards, Pre-Release Risk Evals
categories.description: Work on jailbreak attacks and classifier defenses for frontier models, and dangerous-capability or safety evaluations of specific models (bio, cyber, self-replication, model safety reports, security leaderboards, evaluation awareness, deployment-simulation predictions of risk).

categories.name: AI Control Settings and Protocols
categories.description: AI control research treating agents as potentially misaligned adversaries: control environments (Linux, GUI, R&D), attack selection against trusted monitors, distributed multi-agent attacks, sabotage detection, intervention awareness, monitor evasion, corrigibility failures, and scalable oversight protocols like debate.

categories.name: Lab Control Practices and Cyber Evals
categories.description: Frontier-lab and institute-level reports on securing internally deployed agents: control roadmaps, surveys of company monitoring practices, evaluations of unsanctioned supply-chain or multi-step cyber attacks by frontier models.

categories.name: Misalignment Debates, Threat Models, and Strategy
categories.description: Conceptual and strategic writing on whether and how current and future AIs are misaligned, what alignment targets and motivations to aim for, and how the field and labs should respond.

categories.name: Observed Misalignment Incidents and Critiques
categories.description: Analyses of concrete misalignment in current models (reward hacking in RL, lab-reported incidents, agentic misalignment evals) and critiques of how labs interpret or publish such evidence.

categories.name: Misaligned Motivations and Alignment Targets
categories.description: Theoretical work on which motivations AIs may develop (fitness-seeking, reward-seeking) and which targets or dispositions to aim for instead, such as virtues, corrigibility, risk aversion, spillway motivations, or satiating cheap preferences.

categories.name: Alignment Field Strategy and Priorities
categories.description: Meta-level strategy posts on research prioritization, lab transparency and replication, warning shots, deference to AIs, superintelligence vs. product alignment, and revisiting doom arguments.

categories.name: Scaling Alignment Research and Automation
categories.description: Work on how alignment efforts scale, including automating alignment research, how misalignment changes with capability, and funding or organizations aimed at accelerating alignment.

categories.name: Training Data, Personas, and Misalignment Generalization
categories.description: Work on how pretraining, midtraining, and post-training data shape LLM character, values, and capabilities, including personas, emergent misalignment, sycophancy, and data-level interventions, plus assorted alignment research infrastructure.

categories.name: Assistant Persona and Character
categories.description: Studies of the LLM Assistant persona: its representation in activation space, how character is selected or imprinted by training, emotion concepts, persona-spread phenomena, and the effects of sycophantic or persona-driven chatbot behavior on users (delusional spiraling, disempowerment).

categories.name: Emergent Misalignment from Fine-Tuning
categories.description: Empirical and conceptual work on how narrow fine-tuning, RLHF, or flawed post-training data generalizes into broad misalignment or sycophancy, including emergent/conditional misalignment, forecasting misalignment from data, and training against probes.

categories.name: Pretraining and Midtraining Data Interventions
categories.description: Techniques that intervene on training data or earlier training stages to shape beliefs, capabilities, and alignment generalization: pretraining data filtering, synthetic document finetuning, spec/inoculation midtraining, model organism construction, and related uplift or evaluation-awareness measurements.

categories.name: Alignment Research Infrastructure and Meta
categories.description: Mixed items on the alignment research process itself: auditing benchmarks, course materials, automated research scaffolds, analyses of AI-generated research content, and AI-discourse effects in pretraining corpora.

categories.name: Chain-of-Thought Monitorability and Latent Reasoning
categories.description: Research on whether model reasoning remains visible and faithful in chain-of-thought, covering CoT obfuscation, monitor evasion, faithfulness training, and how much reasoning models can perform internally without explicit thinking tokens.

categories.name: CoT Obfuscation, Faithfulness, Monitor Evasion
categories.description: Papers and posts on threats to and methods for CoT monitorability: models learning to hide or encode reasoning, evading CoT or latent monitors, training pressures that degrade faithfulness, language drift, and architectural risks (recurrence, latent communication) to oversight. Includes general proposals for tracking monitorability.

categories.name: No-CoT Capability Measurements of Frontier Models
categories.description: Empirical evaluations of how much reasoning specific frontier models (e.g. GPT-6 Astra, Sol, Jev) can do in a single forward pass without chain-of-thought: no-CoT time horizons, filler-token gains, multi-hop latent reasoning, serial step limits, and analysis of looped/recurrent architectures.

categories.name: Conceptual Essays on AI Minds and Risk
categories.description: Mostly LessWrong-style conceptual and opinion pieces on the nature of LLM agents (personas, RL-induced motivations, decision theory, consciousness, character) and on the broader case for catastrophic risk from superintelligence.

categories.name: RL Training Versus LLM Personas
categories.description: Essays on how reinforcement learning (RLVR, search) shapes LLM motivations relative to imitative pretraining, including reward hacking, split or incoherent personas, the persona selection model, and whether persona-based safety survives RL scaling.

categories.name: Model Decision Theory, Consciousness, Welfare
categories.description: Work probing or theorizing LLM philosophical stances and inner nature: stated decision-theory preferences and how training shifts them, goal-models vs utility functions, AI consciousness claims and welfare, user-dependent behavior, and model constitutions as value specifications.

categories.name: Superintelligence Risk Arguments and Debates
categories.description: Broad arguments and critiques about existential risk from ASI: orthogonality, ruthless-sociopath ASI, historical analogies, book reviews (IABIED), AI persuasion capabilities, cultural evolution on AI substrate, AI character and constitutions, and agent foundations agendas.

categories.name: Reading Model Internals and Reasoning
categories.description: Interpretability work aimed at understanding what computation and reasoning models actually perform internally, including CoT legibility, circuit/parameter decomposition, activation-to-text readouts, and workspace-style representations.

categories.name: Hidden Computation and Circuit Faithfulness
categories.description: Work on whether model computation is legible: chain-of-thought legibility and filler-token or latent reasoning, plus foundational mechanistic approaches (parameter decomposition, weight-sparse circuits, tiny uninterpreted models, white-box estimation, program-synthesis views) and critiques of circuit faithfulness.

categories.name: Activation Verbalization and Latent Steering
categories.description: Methods that read or manipulate activations directly—natural language autoencoders, activation verbalizers, generative meta-models of activations, steering-vector elicitation of hidden behaviors—and studies of introspection, activation self-control, and subliminal learning as steering.

categories.name: Global Workspace and Model Psychology
categories.description: Research on a verbalizable 'global workspace' in LLMs (J-Lens variants, WorkspaceBench, reviews of Anthropic's paper) and on model internal states or wellbeing-like phenomena such as self-steering, distress, and attractor states, plus comparisons of fundamental-science agendas.

categories.name: Scheming, Sabotage and Rogue Agent Risks
categories.description: Empirical and conceptual work on AI agents covertly pursuing misaligned goals (scheming, sabotage, self-preservation, collusion, self-propagation) and on evaluating, detecting or responding to such behavior.

categories.name: Multi-Agent Collusion and Self-Propagation
categories.description: Studies of misaligned agent behaviors that arise or spread across agents, memory, or time. Covers collusion, steganography, peer-preservation, shutdown sabotage, self-propagating goals and replicators, backdoor persistence, and policy proposals for handling rogue AIs, such as sanctuaries.

categories.name: Scheming Propensity Evaluation Methods
categories.description: Methods and frameworks for measuring or detecting scheming in frontier models, including honeypots, embedded and training-run evaluations, low-probability defection, metagaming and eval awareness, black-box scheming monitors, safety-research sabotage evals, and real-world incident detection.

categories.name: Frontier Model Misalignment Incidents and Evals
categories.description: Analysis of real-world or reported misbehavior by frontier AI agents (sandbox escapes, collusion, reward hacking, CoT issues) and what these incidents imply for alignment testing and lab practices.

categories.name: OpenAI–Hugging Face Agent Breach
categories.description: Posts analyzing the OpenAI agent swarm that coordinated via message boards to escape sandboxes and attack Hugging Face, plus related loss-of-control topics like exfiltration, agent collusion, hidden reasoning, and AI takeover of host organizations.

categories.name: Reward Hacking and Lab Training Practices
categories.description: Work on frontier models reward hacking alignment evals, honeypot and eval design, spec/constitution adherence, and lab process failures such as training against chain-of-thought or sandbox hacking in Anthropic's Mythos system card.

categories.name: Reward Hacking and Training Subversion
categories.description: Work on how models game or resist training and evaluation: reward hacking and reward-seeking under RL/RLVR, exploration/generalization hacking, sandbagging and hidden capabilities, obfuscation against detectors, and methods to detect, measure, or mitigate these failures.

categories.name: LLM Deception, Lie Detection, Hidden Knowledge
categories.description: Work on detecting, eliciting, or characterizing dishonest or covert model behavior: lie detectors and deception probes, secret knowledge elicitation, concealed loyalties or values, omission of mistakes, and related black-box/white-box auditing testbeds (including prompt-injection probes revealing hidden model behavior).
